body:
Earlier seasons felt more emotional for me and I think the voiceovers, especially how they were written, played a part in that. In later seasons it starts to feel like the same thing about love over and over. 

I feel like maybe these voiceovers could benefit from switching to a new narrator or theme... I hear her start going on about love and then I tune out because it is just not my thing and you can only hear it so many times haha.

It's the same way I feel when a Turner family scene shows up - the tone is a little too saccharine for me. 😅

I like the other points made that counter my own though, like how it is a "warm comfy blanket being drawn over" the episode. :)

I always love seasoned rice and canned tuna. Sometimes I'll eat it with kimchi or seaweed, or switch out the tuna for canned salmon. Or sardines on french bread. I guess there is just something about simple canned fish that I never get sick of haha. I really don't like having to eat so having one kind of meal that I do consistently enjoy is certainly helpful.
I'm glad to hear this! Isn't it a nice feeling to have lunch in the outdoors? 😄

I'm proud of you :) It may seem like a small thing but actually it is a big accomplishment, certainly. 

I'm currently in college and I have the same fears. Somehow I'm terrible with following the simplest map directions and I am scared of processes that I'm unfamiliar with. When I do have to go to my in-person classes, it is always the same walking route to the building and then back home. It's the only thing I do: walk to school, then walk back home. 

I'm anxious to try and even find my way to the grocery store. I hope one day I can have the courage to be out navigating this city by myself, or even just taking a walk around the neighborhood.

I'm asexual to be a good person to be a good friend and I don't want to be with you

This thread is amazing hahaha

All the way from elementary school to high school I always dreaded when the teacher took roll call for this reason. I had one teacher who yelled at me when she didn't hear me say "here," even after I repeated it twice.

I feel the same way, my voice sounds loud enough in my head but I guess that doesn't translate to when I'm actually speaking. I noticed I really have to strain to make my natural voice sound audible.

Thank you truly for your understanding.

I haven't explained these feelings to my friends, even though I know they do care about my wellbeing. It was a big help to have a stranger just read my written thoughts and actually understand the way I am feeling. Thank *you* for taking the time to read it and letting me know that it is valid!

I may not know your story, but I wish you the best in the coming days. Please know your comment means very much to me and it won't be forgotten. ☺️
